records.title: What to Provide Before Requesting an Apostille or Authentication
records.question: Home/What to Provide Before Requesting an Apostille or AuthenticationREQUEST-PREPARATION GUIDE · 9 NOVEMBER 2026Start hereIdentify the document’s origin, destination country and receiving party’s instructions before choosing a processing route. The word “apostille” alone does not define the whole request.Start with origin and destinationUSAGov explains that apostilles and authentication certificates verify signatures, stamps or seals on documents, and that the destination affects the required route. Its guidance distinguishes state-issued records from federal records and directs users to the relevant authorities. The U.S. Department of State also publishes separate preparation and submission guidance for authentication and apostille requests.These distinctions make a complete intake important. A document issued by a state authority and one issued by a federal authority should not be routed on the assumption that the same office handles both.The information to collectDocument type: identify the actual record, such as a corporate document, vital record, court record or other specified document.Issuing authority: state who issued or certified it and the state or federal origin. Supply a clear copy for route review when appropriate.Country of use: name the destination and provide the receiving party’s written instructions.Available version: identify whether you hold an original, certified copy, photocopy or electronic record.Additional requirements: include any translation, issuance-date, original-format or consular requirement stated by the recipient.Timing and delivery: give the date needed, delivery destination and any deadline dependency.Do not change the document before reviewAvoid adding a notarization, detaching a certification or mailing an irreplaceable original solely because a generic checklist suggests it. Preparation requirements depend on the document and authority. Confirm what is needed for this specific request before altering or submitting the record.Illustrative request wording“Please review the attached document copy and receiving-party instructions for use in the country identified below. Confirm the required document version, processing authorities, anticipated timing, fees and return-delivery arrangements before we send the original.”What should the confirmation cover?Keep a written record of the agreed route, what the client supplies, any documents to be retrieved, and what is being returned. If recipient requirements remain uncertain, identify the open question rather than promising acceptance. AADS can coordinate the confirmed processing work; the issuing and receiving authorities retain their respective roles.What does an apostille verify?It relates to the signature, seal or official capacity associated with the public document. It should not be represented as validating every factual assertion in that document.Official sources and requirementsUSAGov — Authenticate a U.S. document for use abroad ↗U.S. Department of State — Document authentication ↗Examples illustrate the named jurisdiction or authority; requirements should be confirmed for the actual request.Information is drawn from the official sources linked here. Its UCC forms distinguish information requests from amendments and information statements.Current official UCC guidanceSTATE REQUEST-PREPARATION GUIDE · 10 NOVEMBER 2026Start with the Source MapUse this guide to prepare the request. It maps source types and questions to confirm; it is not a statewide completeness certificate or a legal determination of required scope.Which Source Answers Which Question?Research componentResponsible sourceDefine before orderingCentral UCC recordsWashington Department of LicensingDebtor names, filing references, search type and copiesBusiness entity recordsSecretary of State Corporations and Charities Filing System (CCFS)Entity name or UBI, filing history and the required certificate or copyRecorded property documentsThe responsible county recording officeProperty, instrument references, owner period and copiesCourt case information and documentsWashington court search resources and the court of recordCourt, names, period, case number and underlying documentsUse the Correct State OfficeWashington’s UCC filing and search guidance is published by the Department of Licensing. Corporate entity records are maintained through the Secretary of State’s CCFS. These are separate systems; an entity-status lookup is not a UCC search.Keep the Acknowledgment and Search Result TogetherProvide the filing acknowledgment and number, together with any separately requested search-to-reflect requirements, so your reviewing team receives the appropriate evidence.Check County and Court CoverageThurston County’s recording guidance is one example of a county property source and distinguishes indexed information from documents available online. Washington Courts also explains that its name/case search is reference information; the official case record and document copies are held by the court of record.Request ChecklistExact debtor names and the Department of Licensing UCC request type.Legal entity name, UBI if known and the exact CCFS document or status certificate needed.County, property identifiers and any known recording references.Court and case information, period, dockets and copies needed.Filing acknowledgment, search through-date requirement, client reference and deadline.Example Request“Please quote a Washington Department of Licensing UCC search for [exact name], with [certification/copies], and separately retrieve [entity document] from CCFS. For [county/property], include [specified records]. For court work, identify [court/period] and the documents required. Keep each source and through date distinct.”Make the Result AssessableAsk for a report identifying the exact names and property, sources and criteria used, covered period or through date, located references, supporting copies and any outstanding items. Online coverage, authentication, historical records and source response times vary. Scope, source fees and anticipated timing are confirmed for the actual request.Answers for Your RequestDoes Washington’s Secretary of State handle the central UCC search described here?Washington’s Department of Licensing provides the central UCC filing and search service. The Secretary of State’s CCFS is the separate source for corporate entity records.Does the Washington name-and-case search provide the full official case file?Washington Courts states that the search is reference information. The court of record maintains the official case record, and requested copies should be obtained through the appropriate court process.Official sources and requirementsWashington Department of Licensing — UCC filing and searches ↗Washington Secretary of State — CCFS records tools ↗Washington Courts — name and case search limits ↗Thurston County Auditor — property records ↗Examples describe the named authority. records.title: Zoning Letters, Certificates of Occupancy and Permit Copies: Preparing Your Request
records.question: Home/Zoning Letters, Certificates of Occupancy and Permit Copies: Preparing Your RequestREQUEST-PREPARATION GUIDE · 10 NOVEMBER 2026Start HereIdentify the property, responsible authority and exact document or question. Zoning responses, occupancy records and permit copies are separate requests.Identify the Correct AuthorityProvide the address, parcel number, city and county. Identify the department or jurisdiction already known to be responsible. A mailing address alone may not identify the office that holds zoning or building records.For a Zoning Verification LetterState the current or intended use and the specific questions the recipient wants answered. Supply the recipient’s wording or checklist when available. Do not assume a general zoning letter answers every question about a proposed use, variances or compliance.For Occupancy or Permit RecordsIdentify whether you need an existing certificate of occupancy, permit copy, inspection record or another named document. Provide permit numbers, construction dates and prior addresses when known. Ask the authority to identify unavailable documents rather than assuming every building has the same records.A Hillsborough County ExampleAvailable records and retrieval procedures are confirmed with the responsible jurisdiction.A Useful Request“For [address/parcel], please obtain [specific letter or existing record]. The intended use is [use]; the recipient needs answers to [questions]. Known permits or dates are [details]. Please confirm the responsible authority, fees, anticipated timing and any record limits.”Describe the Results and Documents AccuratelyAn existing occupancy certificate or permit copy is evidence from the issuing authority’s records. Obtaining the copy does not independently approve a new use or certify all work at the property. Keep any legal or technical assessment with the client’s advisers.Official sources and requirementsHillsborough County — Zoning verifications ↗Hillsborough County — Building permitting records ↗Examples describe the named authority; confirm current requirements for the actual request.Information is drawn from the official sources linked here.
